responsibility: Implements the x86 target hook used by GCC’s Rust front end to publish architecture and CPU-feature information. The file defines `ix86_rust_target_cpu_info`, which inspects x86 backend feature flags such as 32/64-bit mode, SSE/AVX generations, BMI, FMA, RNG, XSAVE, and related extensions, then emits Rust `target_arch` and `target_feature` entries through `rust_add_target_info` so Rust conditional compilation sees the active x86 target capabilities.
same_name_distinction: This is the implementation file in the i386-rust pair: it contains the executable x86-specific logic for `ix86_rust_target_cpu_info`, walking backend `TARGET_*` flags and emitting Rust `target_arch`/`target_feature` values. Unlike `i386-rust.h`, it does not define the hook macro interface; it provides the function body used by that interface.
